metadata.note: The Portland and Rochester main line, Portland ME - Gorham - Bar Mills - Alfred - Springvale - Rochester NH, and its predecessor the York and Cumberland. Drawn from research/branches/portland_and_rochester_railroad.txt in the site repo (DanielMConnolly/historical-trains), researched 2026-10-14; only the report's drawable spans are drawn. Rule 4: one feature per drawable span and operator - York and Cumberland (Portland - Gorham 1851-1865, Gorham - Bar Mills 1853-1865), Portland and Rochester (Portland - Bar Mills 1865-1900, Bar Mills - Springvale 1870-1900, Springvale - Rochester 1871-1900), Boston and Maine (Portland - Rochester 1900-1932). The P&R Portland - Bar Mills span is drawn as two features because the Portland approach changed in 1891: Preble Street terminal 1865-1891, Union Station 1891-1900. Passenger service ended 25 June 1932; nothing after is drawn (Rule 1).

source_conflicts: Operator 1886-1900: WP-WNR says the B&M's 1 Jan 1886 lease of the Worcester, Nashua & Rochester 'also included the continuation from Rochester to Portland' (B&M operator from 1886); WP-PR says the P&R 'stayed independent' under B&M stock control (1880s per WP-PR, 1890 per WP-ML; the Osher Map Library calls it B&M-controlled in 1889), and NCS gives the P&R's operating span as 1882-1900, with the merger/sale to the B&M on 1 Jan 1900. Drawn with the split at 1900; NOT settled.
Opening to Gorham: early December 1850 as announced (Eastern Times 28 Nov 1850) vs 1851 (WP-ML and secondary sources). Drawn from 1851, the later end of the bracket.
York and Cumberland -> Portland and Rochester reorganisation: 1 Nov 1865 (WP-PR, WP-YC) vs 1867 (WP-WNR). Drawn at 1865.
The existing B&M research file (boston_and_maine_railroad.txt [19]) says 'B&M lease 1900'; WP-PR and NCS describe the 1900 event as a merger/sale, not a lease.
not_yet_sourced: Who ran the trains 1886-1900: the B&M via the 1886 WN&R lease, or the B&M-controlled but independent P&R. A B&M or P&R public timetable of 1887-1899, or the Maine Railroad Commissioners' reports, would settle whether the P&R -> B&M split belongs at 1886.
Whether the York and Cumberland actually opened to Gorham in December 1850 as announced; drawn from 1851.
York and Cumberland traction: no source read says the 1850s trains were steam-hauled; nothing hints at horses either.
Whether any section beyond Bar Mills (e.g. to Alfred) carried passengers before December 1870.

The day 25 June 1932 rests on one secondary citation (Lindsell 2000 p.82 via Wikipedia); the year 1932 is also given by the Sanford-Springvale Historical Society. Whether a Portland - Westbrook/Gorham local outlived the June 1932 cut was not established.

Portland terminal: the Y&C's original terminal (Fowler 'Portland (P&R) (1850>1860)'), the Preble Street depot site, and whether pre-1891 trains reached it over the Maine Central via Woodfords or over the P&R's own Deering Jct - Preble St line (abandoned 1911). The last passenger year at Preble Street is unknown.
All headway_min and avg_speed_kmh values are estimates; the only frequency found is c.1909 (three trains each way past Springvale).
Not read directly: Lindsell 2000, Karr 2010, Johnson 1951 (all via Wikipedia only).
omitted: Back Cove connection to the Grand Trunk at Portland & Rochester Junction (1874): no evidence of P&R passenger trains on it (report block [8], drawable NONE).
Deering Junction - Preble Street as a separate feature (report block [7], drawable NONE); it is drawn only as the pre-1891 Portland approach of the main-line features.
Sanford and Eastern Railroad 1949-1961: freight only (Official Guide Nov 1951 'Daily Freight Service Only'), Rule 1 (report block [9]).

properties.geometry_quality: Portland (Preble Street) - Gorham: traced 11.1 mi against a documented c.10.5 mi (WP-ML route map, Preble St MP 0 - Gorham MP 10.5); Fowler gives 11.9 mi Gorham - Union Station. Approximated (straight) legs: three short gap-bridges between disconnected OSM fragments of the B&M-tagged grade - 0.12 mi (197 m) at 43.680 N, -70.430 east of Gorham; 0.04 mi (64 m) at 43.682 N, -70.386 west of Westbrook; and the eastern part of a 0.43 mi (686 m) bridge at Gorham (43.676 N, -70.445). Total under 0.6 mi. PORTLAND APPROACH (pre-1891): drawn from Deering Junction over the Maine Central through Woodfords, then onto the Back Cove line (OHM way 200673681, Portland Terminal Co. 'Main Line') to the Preble Street crossing at 43.6597 N, -70.2676; a ~75 m sidestep joins the MEC main to that line just north of Union Station. The Preble Street depot site is placed at the crossing, not located from a source. Fowler's Deering Jct - Preble St distance (3.6 mi via the MEC) matches this route; whether the trains instead used the P&R's own Deering Jct - Preble St line (2.5 mi, abandoned 1911, WP-ML) is not established. The OHM track is the later Portland Terminal Co. layout, so this is a LATER alignment than the era it is drawn for. The Y&C's original Portland terminal (Fowler 'Portland (P&R) 1850>1860') is not located and is drawn as the same Preble Street approach. Section ends are the projections onto the line of Gorham (0.24 km off), Bar Mills (0.47 km off, at the Saco River crossing) and Springvale (0.45 km off); station sites themselves were not pinned. ERA CAVEAT: the whole line is drawn on the grade as OSM maps it, i.e. as it stood before its 1952/1961 abandonment; any 1850s-1870s alignment differences are unmapped and not drawn.

segments.note: York and Cumberland trains Portland - Saccarappa (Westbrook) - Cumberland Mills - Gorham. The Eastern Times (Bath) of 28 Nov 1850 announced the line 'will be opened to Gorham, early in December' 1850; the P&R main-line article and secondary sources give 1851. Whether the December 1850 opening happened is not confirmed, so this is drawn from 1851, the later end of the bracket. 1865 is an era boundary, not an end of service: the company was reorganised as the Portland and Rochester on 1 Nov 1865 (WP-PR, WP-YC; WP-WNR says 1867 - conflict recorded in metadata). The 1851-52 F.O.J. Smith v. Poor litigation over the presidency was a control fight, not a service break. No source says outright that the first trains were locomotive-hauled; nothing hints at animal traction either. Headway 720 (about two trains a day each way) is an estimate; no Y&C timetable was read.
sources: Segment-level: Eastern Times 28 Nov 1850 p.3 for the announced December 1850 opening; Wikipedia (P&R main line) for 1851; Wikipedia (P&R; Y&C) for the 1 Nov 1865 reorganisation; Fowler table 55 lists 'Portland (P&R) (1850>1860) x'. Headway NOT SOURCED (estimate).

segments.note: Portland and Rochester trains over the former York and Cumberland, from the reorganisation of 1 Nov 1865 (WP-PR, WP-YC; WP-WNR and other notes say 1867 - conflict recorded). The 1881/82 reorganisation as a new Portland and Rochester corporation (effective 1 May 1882, NCS) did not change who ran the trains and is not a split. Ends 1891 only because the Portland approach changes: a branch to Union Station opened in 1891 (WP-PR), and from then the companion feature portland-rochester-portland-bar-mills draws the Union Station approach. The Preble Street terminal's last passenger year is not established (B&M abandoned Deering Jct - Preble St in 1911). A Back Cove connection to the Grand Trunk opened 1874 (WP-PR); no evidence that P&R passenger trains used it, so it is not drawn. Headway 600 is an estimate; no P&R timetable was read.

segments.note: Portland and Rochester trains into Union Station, Portland, after the 1891 connection (WP-PR). B&M took stock control in the 1880s/1890 (WP-PR; WP-ML says 1890), but stock control is not an operator change; the P&R was merged into the Boston and Maine on 1 Jan 1900 (WP-PR, NCS), which ends this feature. CONFLICT: WP-WNR says the B&M's 1 Jan 1886 lease of the Worcester, Nashua & Rochester 'also included the continuation from Rochester to Portland', which would make the B&M the operator from 1886; WP-PR says the P&R 'stayed independent' and NCS gives the P&R's operating span as 1882-1900. Split at 1900 per the research report; unresolved (see metadata). Headway 480 is an estimate.

Routing was held off the B&M Eastern Trail / Portland Subdivision and the MEC Mountain Division by waypoints on the P&R grade. Portland end on the Maine Central (Deering Jct - Woodfords) and Portland Terminal Co. tracks from OSM and OHM. Waypoints checked against the line (Nominatim gives admin/neighbourhood centroids in Maine): every town waypoint within 0.5 km of the drawn line. OHM used for geometry only, never for dates.
properties.geometry_quality: Portland (Union Station) - Rochester: traced 52.4 mi against a documented 54.2 mi (Fowler 148.5 Union Station - 94.3 Rochester); WP-ML gives 52.5 mi from Preble Street. Approximated (straight) legs: gap-bridges between disconnected OSM fragments of the B&M-tagged grade, 1.6 mi in all - 0.34 mi (365 + 189 m) at 43.653-43.656 N, -70.478 to -70.473; 0.66 mi (439 + 628 m) at 43.662-43.669 N, -70.465 to -70.456; 0.43 mi (686 m) at Gorham (43.676 N, -70.445); 0.12 mi (197 m) at 43.680 N, -70.430; 0.04 mi (64 m) at 43.682 N, -70.386. PORTLAND APPROACH (from 1891): Deering Junction - Woodfords over the Maine Central, ending on the Portland Terminal Co. main (OHM 'Main Line 01') at 43.6537 N, -70.2806 beside the Union Station site. The OSM grade is sparsely noded in places (raw vertices up to 1.1 km apart on tangent track, e.g. Waterboro and East Lebanon), drawn as the tangents the source gives. Rochester end at the junction of the P&R grade with the B&M Conway line (43.3069 N, -70.9729); the Rochester station site itself is not pinned. ERA CAVEAT: the whole line is drawn on the grade as OSM maps it, i.e. as it stood before its 1952/1961 abandonment; any 1850s-1870s alignment differences are unmapped and not drawn.

segments.note: Boston and Maine trains after the merger of the Portland and Rochester on 1 Jan 1900 (WP-PR, NCS), worked as part of the Worcester, Nashua & Portland Division. Possibly B&M-operated from 1886 (WP-WNR) - see metadata; not drawn earlier for lack of agreement. c.1909 six passenger trains (three each way) passed Springvale daily (Sanford-Springvale Historical Society), the only frequency found; headway 360 is derived from that count spread over the day, an estimate. Passenger service ended 25 June 1932 (Lindsell 2000 p.82, via WP-ML); the Sanford-Springvale Historical Society independently gives 1932, blaming the automobile. Whether a Portland - Westbrook/Gorham local survived the June 1932 cut was not established; nothing shows any later service. Context only, not drawn (Rule 1): B&M freight continued; the line was sold in 1949 to the Sanford & Eastern (Pinsly), which ran 'Daily Freight Service Only' (Official Guide, Nov 1951 table) and abandoned Rochester - Springvale in 1952 and the rest in 1961 (Karr 2010 via WP-ML). The B&M abandoned Deering Jct - Preble Street in 1911.
sources: Segment-level: Wikipedia (P&R) and Nashua City Station for the 1 Jan 1900 merger; Wikipedia (P&R main line) citing Lindsell 2000 p.82 for the 25 Jun 1932 end; Sanford-Springvale Historical Society for the year 1932 and the c.1909 frequency; Official Guide Feb 1952 (Nov 1951 table and index daggers) for freight-only status in 1951. Headway derived from the c.1909 train count (estimate).
